availableCommands.name: rust-best-practices
availableCommands.description: Write idiomatic, robust, maintainable Rust. Use this skill whenever you write, review, refactor, debug, or explain Rust code: new crates, modules, functions, structs, traits, error types, async code, unsafe or FFI code, Cargo.toml, tests, or rustdoc. Trigger on any mention of Rust, cargo, crates, .rs files, the borrow checker, lifetimes, traits, clippy, or rustfmt, even when the user does not ask for "best practices" or "idiomatic" code. Synthesized from the Google Rust Style Guide, the Rust API Guidelines, Effective Rust, Rust Design Patterns, and Microsoft's Pragmatic Rust Guidelines.

availableCommands.name: rust-review
availableCommands.description: Review existing Rust code for idiom, API design, error handling, safety, and maintainability, and produce a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and gives a concrete fix. Use this whenever the user asks to review, audit, critique, grade, or "check" Rust code, a crate, a module, a .rs file, a diff, or a pull request, or asks what is wrong with their Rust or how to make it more idiomatic, even if they don't say "review". Pairs with the rust-best-practices skill, which covers writing new code.
